name: Astra / ChatGPT Capability Factory
one_liner: Discover economically useful capabilities, mine GitHub before coding, assemble them, validate them, then compile them into ChatGPT/MCP/web/API surfaces.
core_thesis: As model cognition becomes abundant, a large fraction of valuable software capabilities can be assembled from existing open-source components. The winning factory searches for demand, specifies an atomic capability, mines GitHub aggressively, composes the best parts, fills gaps, validates behavior deterministically, and publishes where users already express intent—especially ChatGPT.
why_now: ChatGPT-native app/plugin distribution is newer than most model training data and can remove large portions of standalone SaaS distribution and UI cost.
user: Operator who wants a repeatable capability factory
job: Turn a grounded opportunity into a tested ChatGPT-native capability with minimal bespoke code.
distribution: ChatGPT apps/plugins first; same capability compiled to MCP, website, API and x402.
moat: Capability ontology + GitHub component graph + deterministic eval corpus + cross-build trajectories.
falsifiers: Plugin discovery does not provide meaningful distribution.
GitHub assembly is slower or less reliable than clean-room generation.
Capabilities cannot share enough infrastructure to compound.

success_definition: All 12 checkpoints PROVEN on live evidence, with no unresolved critical H-task or security gate.

repo_binding.polling: GitHub snapshots are implementation evidence only; checkpoint proof comes from validator receipts.

software_substitution_test.counterfactual: OpenAI/platform vendors ship perfect software for every reproducible feature in this project tomorrow.
surviving_value: internal speed advantage when pointed at scarce assets controlled elsewhere
software_substitution_test.rationale: Assume platform vendors make protocol compilation trivial. Keep Astra only as the internal software factory surrounding scarce assets.

underengineer.rule: Choose the earliest real-world event that increases controlled scarce state; build only its prerequisites plus safety and verification.
underengineer.scarce_state_target: Manufacture one interface required by a live asset campaign
underengineer.minimal_live_product: Given an already-owned scarce asset and behavior contract, search existing components, assemble the smallest interface, and pass one active capability probe.

steps.action: Bind to a scarce asset owned by another campaign
steps.acceptance: Asset ID and behavior contract are explicit.

steps.action: Search and select reusable components before bespoke code
Actively probe the interface against the real asset

underengineer.graduation_rule: A live campaign acquires or monetizes scarce state through the generated interface.
underengineer.kill_or_rethink_rule: If the interface is not required for a live scarce-asset event, do not build it.
underengineer.project_manager_invariant: A feature may enter NOW only if it is necessary to reach the first real moat event, required for safety/verification, or empirically unblocks that path.
underengineer.observation_pause: After the first live moat event, stop expanding and inspect customer/outcome evidence before choosing the next feature.

full_roadmap_policy: The original checkpoint ladder is a capability library, not default build order. UNDERENGINEER chooses the live minimum path.

experiment_strategy.learning_goal: Use as cheap probe/manufacturing infrastructure only when pulled by an asset campaign.
